scope: Ordinary-only offline frozen-parameter diagnostic. No parameter fit, controller edit, independent-validation output access or hardware.
questions: Does changing RPM observations alter the existing forced-position replay?
Do spring and cross-damping terms suppress measured projected-encoder synchronization dynamics?
Is a simple zero-lag integer-RPM observation hypothesis consistent with complete motion displacement?
fixedCases: spring zero, all other fitted coefficients fixed
cross-damping zero, all other fitted coefficients fixed
spring and cross-damping zero, all other fitted coefficients fixed
data: Same ordinary Q2S68012 training record. Complete20s single initial state; exact1ms moving commands, explicit unverified hold-mean ZOH.
motionMetrics: Original native40ms phase2..5 and exact8000 moving endpoint positions. No measured-future-state injection.
RPMProbe: Mutate only an in-memory copy of all decoded RPM samples to constant100. Actual command arrays and encoder observations unchanged. This tests the replay dependency graph, not the physical controller's response to RPM.
RPMConsistencyAssumption: Two declared zero-lag hypotheses for interval-mean motor speed: nearest integer gives +/-0.5rpm bin; floor integer gives [rpm,rpm+1]. Integrate bins over actual dt. These simplified interval-mean observation assumptions are not certified hardware sampling/filter/quantizer models.
encoderEnvelope: For these conditional bin tests only, allow +/-one native encoder count at each endpoint. This is a numerical-bin assumption, not independently measured carriage accuracy.
verification: Native baseline metrics match round66; common-mode symmetric fixture invariant under coupling knockouts; independent JS metric recomputation from400storedpoints and per-window RPM bounds.
interpretation: A favorable fixed knockout is mechanism sensitivity on training input, not newly calibrated plant, physical parameter proof, method superiority or closed-loop validation. Do not pick a final physical controller from it.
